transcript.content: Hi, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

I came in because I’ve been having these thoughts like… maybe it’d be easier if I just didn’t wake up. I haven’t made any plan to hurt myself, but it’s been on my mind enough that I figured I should talk to someone.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most days?
Yeah… most days lately. After that burst of energy wore off, it was like somebody pulled the plug on me. I’d just sit at the table staring at my coffee, feeling empty… and pretty ashamed of myself.
During that burst of energy, did you feel unusually up or unusually irritable?
Yeah. Right after I got fired, I felt… oddly fired up, like I was going to prove everybody wrong. But I was also really irritable, snapping at people over small stuff, even at the coffee shop.
During that burst of energy, did you need much less sleep than usual?
Yeah. There were a few nights where I only slept maybe two or three hours, and I’d still get up feeling wide awake, like I had plenty of energy and didn’t need to slow down.
During that burst of energy, were you doing a lot more activities or projects than usual?

Yeah, definitely more than usual. I was jumping from filling out job applications to sketching woodworking ideas, then rewriting my resume again. I’d barely sit still long enough to finish one thing before I was onto the next.
During that energized period, did you feel unusually confident or like you could do things other people couldn’t?

Yeah, I did. I had this feeling like I could walk into any store in the district and run it better than the managers there. Like getting fired somehow proved I knew more than everyone else, which sounds strange now, but at the time I really believed it.
About how many days in a row did that fired-up, high-energy period last?
It was about three weeks straight after I got fired. It kind of stayed up like that most days during that stretch.
During that three-week fired-up period, did your behavior cause serious problems in your life or relationships?

Yeah, it did. I fell behind on bills and missed some callbacks and appointments I should’ve kept up with. I was trying to look for work, but I couldn’t keep it steady or organized, even though I really needed a job. Even stuff around the house got sloppy, and at some point I knew I wasn’t just going to fix it by trying harder.
During that fired-up period, did you have any beliefs that other people said were unrealistic or not true?

Yeah. I believed I could walk into pretty much any store in the district and run it better than the people already managing it. At the time it felt obvious to me, like getting fired somehow meant I understood things better than everyone else. Looking back, I can see how unrealistic that sounded.
During that fired-up period, did you hear or see things that other people couldn't?

Yeah. There was one time when I was really wound up, I heard my old store manager’s voice, clear as day, like it was coming over an intercom. He was telling me to “move the display,” but I was just sitting alone in my kitchen. It shook me up some.
Did you ever hear that voice at a time when you were not in that fired-up, high-energy state?

No, not that I remember. That store-manager voice only happened during those wired weeks after I got fired. Once I came down and hit that low period, it stopped. I was mostly just embarrassed about how sure I’d been about everything.
